step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates NuData Security's machine learning and real-time fraud detection pipeline on AWS. Requests enter through API Gateway to Lambda (representing the rules engine), which invokes real-time predictive model endpoints hosted on SageMaker. Concurrently, historical data stored in Amazon Redshift is exported to Amazon S3. S3 event notifications (via SNS) trigger AWS Step Functions, which orchestrates various SageMaker jobs including model training, hyperparameter tuning, and batch transforms.

graph.name: NuData Security Real-Time Machine Learning Fraud Detection Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture shows NuDetect real-time scoring via API Gateway, Lambda, and SageMaker alongside an automated model training flow using Redshift, S3, Step Functions, and SageMaker.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: REST API entry point for customer web, mobile, and server traffic.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Executes the rules engine microservices returning responses within 200 ms.

nodes.name: Redshift
nodes.notes: Data warehouse containing aggregated transactional and behavioral data.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores exported training datasets from Redshift.

nodes.name: Step Functions
nodes.notes: Orchestrates machine learning workflows based on dataset paths.

nodes.name: SageMaker
nodes.notes: Handles model training, hyperparameter tuning, batch transform, and real-time endpoint hosting.
